test_ideas: In the local lab, try accessing another user's basket/order as a different logged-in local account and note whether the server enforces ownership.
Try requesting admin-only pages or functions as a regular local user and record the server response.
Check whether changing an ID in a request (e.g. basket or user ID) returns another account's data.
Check whether the local instance is served over plain HTTP and what sensitive data the login/checkout forms submit.
Look for sensitive data exposed in responses, local storage, or client-side code in the local lab.
Note password policy and storage behaviour only as documented by the local app itself.
Test the local search and login inputs with ordinary special characters and observe error handling (no payloads against any real site).
Check whether input is reflected unsanitised in a page in the local lab.
Note any database or command error messages returned by the local app.
Walk a business flow end to end (e.g. checkout, password reset) and note missing limits, checks, or confirmations.
Check whether a flow can be abused by skipping steps or replaying a step in the local lab.
Record whether rate limits or abuse controls appear on sensitive flows.
Review response headers, error pages, and default settings of the local instance.
Check for debug endpoints, verbose errors, or unnecessary features left enabled locally.
Note directory or file listings exposed by the local instance, if any.
List the local instance's version and its client-side libraries as reported by the app itself.
Compare those versions against public advisories and note any known-vulnerable component.
Record whether the local Docker image is the current release or an old pinned one.
Test the local login for account enumeration via differing error messages.
Check session behaviour: logout, expiry, and reuse of an old session token in the local lab.
Note whether weak or default local test credentials are accepted.
Check how the local instance verifies updates, plugins, or uploaded content, if applicable.
Note whether unsigned or untrusted content can be loaded by the local app.
Record CI/CD or supply-chain observations only for your own local build.
Trigger failed logins and suspicious actions locally and check what the app logs.
Check whether logs are viewable, tamper-evident, or alerted on in the local setup.
Note gaps: events that should be logged but produce no record.
Find any feature in the local lab that fetches a URL or image on the server's behalf.
Test it only with local, safe destinations (e.g. localhost services you control) and record the response.
Note whether private/internal addresses are blocked by the local app.
